title: Monday Move
headline: I built an agent that posted only the competitor news it could prove
summary: A Claude Code scheduled task that read a week of news on seven competitors every Monday and turned it into one move for the team, with a source behind every signal.
description: A weekly agent that read seven competitors' news and led each Slack post with one move for the team, every signal sourced and dated.
facts: Builder: wrote the prompt and ran it
Claude Code, web search, Slack, Notion
outcome: Nine digests led with a verified move, and quiet weeks said "no verified signals" instead of filling the slot.

hero.alt: A Slack post headed with this week's move, followed by a high-impact and a medium-impact signal, each with a date, an angle and a source link, and a footer counting 2 verified and 4 discarded.
hero.caption: The Monday post, rebuilt with invented companies.

story: My team at work needed to know what seven competitors did each week. That news is messy: articles get republished, and some never say when the event happened.

Each Monday at 8am the agent searched the past seven days and rated every finding. High meant it could threaten revenue or open a market; Medium, worth watching or enough to sway a deal or two; Low, noise that went to the Notion log and never the post.

calls.why: Three verified signals made a good run, and eight unverified ones a failed run. Eight looks busier, so the prompt ranked it lower.
Before searching, the agent wrote out the seven-day window. Each item then needed a source and a confirmed event date inside it, or it was dropped, never swapped for a weaker one.
What the prompt told it about each competitor could never come back as a finding.
Each post opened with the single most actionable signal, verb-first, so the team had one thing to do.

images.caption: Verified signals went to a log; each run also listed what it dropped and why.
